purpose: Pyrazinamide is used to treat tuberculosis (TB), a serious bacterial infection that mainly affects the lungs. It is almost always used in combination with other antibiotics, not alone. Completing the full course of treatment is very important to cure TB and prevent it from coming back.
how_it_works: Pyrazinamide works by getting inside the TB bacteria and disrupting their ability to make the substances they need to survive. It creates an acidic environment inside the bacteria that essentially stops them from growing and eventually kills them. It is especially helpful in the early phase of TB treatment because it can reach bacteria hiding in hard-to-treat areas of the body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is joint pain or aching, which can affect your muscles and joints. You may also notice nausea, vomiting, or an upset stomach. Some people experience increased sensitivity to sunlight, so use sunscreen when going outdoors. Loss of appetite is also fairly common.
warnings: This medication can cause serious liver problems. Watch for warning signs like yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark-colored urine, severe stomach pain, or unusual tiredness, and contact your doctor right away if these occur. Pyrazinamide can raise uric acid levels in your blood, which may trigger gout in some people. Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, gout, or diabetes before starting this medicine. Never stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel better.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is based on your body weight, typically around 15 to 30 mg per kilogram of body weight taken once daily by mouth. A common dose for most adults is 1,000 to 2,000 mg per day. Your doctor will determine the exact dose and schedule for you. It is usually taken for the first 2 months of a standard TB treatment course. Always take it exactly as prescribed.
